draft.overview: Haloalkanes (alkyl halides) are organic compounds containing at least one halogen atom bound to an sp3 hybridized carbon atom. The electronegativity difference between carbon and halogen renders the C-X bond polar, giving rise to electrophilic character at carbon and enabling nucleophilic substitution and elimination reactions. Understanding preparation methods, C-X bond polarity, and SN1/SN2 substitution mechanisms is essential for mastering organic synthesis in JEE Main Chemistry.

concepts.title: Nature of the C-X Bond
concepts.explanation: Halogens are more electronegative than carbon, imparting a partial positive charge (delta+) on carbon and a partial negative charge (delta-) on halogen. C-X bond length increases down the halogen group (C-F < C-Cl < C-Br < C-I), leading to a decrease in bond dissociation enthalpy. Consequently, reactivity of alkyl halides in substitution reactions generally follows the order: R-I > R-Br > R-Cl > R-F.

concepts.title: SN2 Mechanism (Bimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution)
concepts.explanation: SN2 is a concerted, single-step reaction involving backside attack of a nucleophile on the electrophilic carbon. It proceeds via a pentacoordinate transition state leading to complete inversion of stereochemical configuration (Walden inversion). The rate depends on both substrate and nucleophile concentration. Reactivity decreases with steric hindrance: Methyl > Primary > Secondary > Tertiary.

concepts.title: SN1 Mechanism (Unimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution)
concepts.explanation: SN1 is a two-step mechanism where the slow rate-determining step involves heterolytic cleavage of the C-X bond to yield a planar carbocation intermediate. Nucleophilic attack then occurs rapidly from either face, leading to racemization (or partial inversion). Substrate reactivity depends on carbocation stability: Allylic/Benzylic >= Tertiary > Secondary > Primary > Methyl.

concepts.title: Methods of Preparation
concepts.explanation: Alkyl halides can be prepared from alcohols using phosphorus halides (PCl3, PCl5), thionyl chloride (SOCl2 in pyridine, preferred due to gaseous by-products HCl and SO2), or halogen acids (HX/ZnCl2). Other important routes include free-radical halogenation of alkanes, electrophilic addition of HX to alkenes, and halogen exchange reactions like Finkelstein (NaI/acetone) and Swarts (AgF/SbF3) reactions.

formulaRegister.label: SN2 Reaction Rate Law
formulaRegister.applicability: Determines kinetics of bimolecular nucleophilic substitution reactions.

formulaRegister.label: SN1 Reaction Rate Law
formulaRegister.applicability: Determines kinetics of unimolecular nucleophilic substitution reactions.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: SN1 reactions always yield complete 100% racemization.
commonMisconceptions.correction: In practice, SN1 reactions often produce slight inversion over retention because the leaving group shields the front side momentarily as an ion pair before full solvation.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Primary alkyl halides never undergo SN1 substitution under any condition.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Primary allylic and primary benzylic halides undergo rapid SN1 substitution because the resulting carbocations are strongly resonance-stabilized.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Dipole moment strictly decreases down the group from C-F to C-I.
commonMisconceptions.correction: C-Cl has a slightly higher dipole moment than C-F (CH3Cl > CH3F > CH3Br > CH3I) because the significantly larger C-Cl bond distance outweighs the higher electronegativity of fluorine.

workedExamples.problem: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of reactivity towards SN1 reaction: (I) 2-bromobutane, (II) 1-bromobutane, (III) 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
steps: Step 1: Identify the carbocation intermediate formed after C-Br bond cleavage for each substrate.
Step 5: Order of carbocation stability is 3rd degree > 2nd degree > 1st degree.
Step 6: Therefore, SN1 reactivity increases in the order: (II) < (I) < (III).

workedExamples.problem: Predict the major organic product formed when (R)-2-bromobutane reacts with aqueous KOH via SN2 pathway.
steps: Step 1: Identify the mechanism: SN2 mechanism proceeds via backside attack by hydroxide ion.
Step 2: SN2 reaction leads to complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion).
Step 3: Inversion of (R)-2-bromobutane converts the absolute configuration from R to S.
Step 4: The nucleophile -OH replaces -Br with inverted stereochemistry.

selfChecks.question:
Which reagent is most preferred for preparing alkyl chlorides from alcohols because the by-products are gaseous?
A) PCl5
B) SOCl2
C) HCl / ZnCl2
D) PCl3
selfChecks.answer: B) SOCl2. Thionyl chloride (SOCl2) is preferred because the by-products (SO2 and HCl) are gases and escape easily, leaving behind pure alkyl chloride.

selfChecks.question:
Which of the following compounds reacts fastest via SN2 mechanism?
A) (CH3)3C-Br
B) (CH3)2CH-Br
C) CH3-CH2-Br
D) CH3-Br
selfChecks.answer: D) CH3-Br. Methyl bromide has minimal steric hindrance, allowing the nucleophile to perform backside attack most rapidly in an SN2 reaction.

selfChecks.question:
Finkelstein reaction is best utilized for synthesis of which haloalkane class?
A) Alkyl fluorides
B) Alkyl iodides
C) Alkyl chlorides
D) Aryl bromides
selfChecks.answer: B) Alkyl iodides. Finkelstein reaction involves reacting alkyl chlorides or bromides with NaI in dry acetone to prepare alkyl iodides.
